source: Dallas City Code ch. 51P, Article 393 (City Attorney's codified article, April 2026)

sections.title: Legislative History
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-393.101. LEGISLATIVE HISTORY.

PD 393 was established by Ordinance No. 21918, passed by the Dallas City Council on December 8, 1993. Ordinance No. 21918 amended Ordinance No. 19455, Chapter 51A of the Dallas City Code, as amended. Ordinance No. 21918 was amended by Ordinance No. 23805, passed by the Dallas City Council on February 24, 1999. (Ord. Nos. 19455; 21918; 23805; 25850)

sections.title: Property Location And Size
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-393.102. PROPERTY LOCATION AND SIZE.

PD 393 is established on property generally located at the southwest corner of Greenville Avenue and Stults Road. The size of PD 393 is approximately 8.032 acres. (Ord. Nos. 21918; 25850)

sections.title: Definitions And Interpretations
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-393.103. DEFINITIONS AND INTERPRETATIONS.

(a) Definitions. Unless otherwise stated, the definitions contained in Chapter 51A apply to this article. In the event of a conflict, this article controls.

(b) Interpretations.

(1) Unless otherwise stated, all references to code articles, divisions, or sections in this article refer to articles, divisions, or sections in Chapter 51A.

(2) Section 51A-2.101, “Interpretations,” applies to this article.

(3) For purposes of determining the applicability of regulations in this article and in Chapter 51A triggered by adjacency or proximity to another zoning district, and for purposes of interpreting the DIR and RAR requirements of Division 51A-4.800, this district is considered to be a residential zoning district. (Ord. Nos. 21918; 25850)

SEC. 51P-393.103.1. EXHIBITS.

The following exhibits are incorporated into this article:

(1) Exhibit 393A: Subarea 1 development and landscape plan.

(2) Exhibit 393B: subarea map.

(3) Exhibit 393C: Subarea 2 conceptual plan. (Ord. 32163)

SEC. 51P-393.103.2. SUBAREAS.

This district is divided into two subareas as shown on the subarea map (Exhibit 393B). (Ord. 32163)

SEC. 51P-393.103.3. SUBAREA 2 CONCEPTUAL PLAN.

Development and use of Subarea 2 must comply with the Subarea 2 conceptual plan (Exhibit 393C). If there is a conflict between the text of this article and the Subarea 2 conceptual plan, the text of this article controls. (Ord. 32163)

sections.title: Development And Landscape Plan
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-393.104. DEVELOPMENT AND LANDSCAPE PLAN.

(a) Subarea 1. Development and use of Subarea 1 must comply with the Subarea 1 development and landscape plan (Exhibit 393A). If there is a conflict between the text of this article and the Subarea 1 development and landscape plan, the text of this article controls.

(b) Subarea 2.

(1) For single family uses, a final plat may serve as the development plan. If there is a conflict between the text of this article and a final plat, the text of this article controls.

(2) For all other uses, a development plan must be approved by the city plan commission before the issuance of any building permit to authorize work in Subarea 2. If there is a conflict between the text of this article and the development plan, the text of this article controls. (Ord. Nos. 23805; 25850; 32163)

sections.title: Main Uses Permitted
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-393.105. MAIN USES PERMITTED.

(a) Community service center.

(b) Handicapped group dwelling unit.

(c) Local utilities.

(d) Single family. (Ord. Nos. 21918; 25850)

sections.title: Accessory Uses
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-393.106. ACCESSORY USES.

As a general rule, an accessory use is permitted in any district in which the main use is permitted. Some specific types of accessory uses, however, due to their unique nature, are subject to additional regulations contained in Section 51A-4.217. For more information regarding accessory uses, consult Section 51A-4.217. (Ord. Nos. 21918; 25850)

sections.title: Yard, Lot, And Space Regulations
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-393.107. YARD, LOT, AND SPACE REGULATIONS.

(Note: The yard, lot, and space regulations in this section must be read together with the yard, lot, and space regulations contained in Division 51A-4.400. In the event of a conflict between this section and Division 51A-4.400, this section controls.)

(a) Front, side, and rear yard.

(1) Subarea 1. All setbacks must comply with the Subarea 1 development and landscape plan.

(2) Subarea 2.

(A) Front yard. Minimum front yard is 15 feet.

(B) Side and rear yard. Minimum side and rear yard is five feet.

(C) Enclosed parking setback. An enclosed parking space must provide a 20- foot setback from the shared access easement line.

(b) Dwelling unit density.

(1) Subarea 1. No maximum dwelling unit density.

(2) Subarea 2. Maximum number of dwelling units is 30.

(c) Floor area ratio.

(1) Maximum floor area ratio for the community service center use is .75.

(2) No maximum floor area ratio for residential uses.

(d) Height. Maximum structure height is 36 feet.

(e) Lot coverage.

(1) Maximum lot coverage is:

(A) 45 percent for residential structures; and

(B) 60 percent for nonresidential structures.

(2) The shared access area may be used to calculate lot coverage.

(f) Lot size.

(1) Subarea 1. Minimum lot area for residential uses is 10,000 square feet.

(2) Subarea 2. Minimum lot area for residential uses is 3,100 square feet.

(3) Shared access area. The shared access area may be used to calculate lot area.

(g) Stories.

(1) Community service center. Maximum number of stories above grade is three.

(2) Residential uses in Subarea 1. No maximum number of stories.

(3) Subarea 2. Maximum number of stories above grade is two. (Ord. Nos. 21918; 25850; 32163)

sections.title: Lighting
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-393.108. LIGHTING.

(a) All building entrances connected with the community service center use must be illuminated. The light sources must be shielded or directed so as to reduce glare or excessive illumination off the premises.

(b) All parking lots connected with the community service center use must be illuminated by pole mounted lights that do not exceed 15 feet in height. Unless otherwise required be regulations contained in the Dallas Development Code, parking lot lights must be turned off within one hour after the facility housing the use is closed.

(c) Lighting for sports fields and activity areas, and residentially adjacent pole lighting must be directed toward the exterior of the use to which it is connected and designed so as not to protrude beyond the boundary of the use. Except as otherwise required by the Dallas Development Code, no such lighting is permitted between the hours of 11:00 p.m. and 6:00 a.m. (Ord. Nos. 21918; 25850)

sections.title: Screening
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-393.109. SCREENING.

A minimum six-foot-high solid screening fence must be provided and maintained along the western and part of the southern boundaries of the Property, as shown on the Subarea 1 development and landscape plan. The screening fence must be designed so as not to permit scaling. (Ord. Nos. 23805; 25850; 32163)

sections.title: Off-Street Parking And Loading
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-393.110. OFF-STREET PARKING AND LOADING.

(a) Consult the use regulations contained in Division 51A-4.200 for the specific off-street parking requirements for each use.

(b) Consult the off-street parking and loading regulations contained in Divisions 51A-4.300 et seq. for information regarding off-street parking and loading generally.

(c) Entrances to parking areas for the community service center use must be locked off and sufficiently barricaded to prevent entry at all times that the facility is closed to the public. (Ord. Nos. 21918; 25850)

sections.title: Environmental Performance Standards
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-393.111. ENVIRONMENTAL PERFORMANCE STANDARDS.

See Article VI. (Ord. Nos. 21918; 25850)

sections.title: Landscaping
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-393.112. LANDSCAPING.

(a) In general. Plant materials must be maintained in a healthy, growing condition.

(b) Subarea 1. Landscaping must be provided as shown on the Subarea 1 development and landscape plan.

(c) Subarea 2. Landscaping must be provided in accordance with Article X. (Ord. Nos. 23805; 25850; 32163)

sections.title: Access
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-393.113. ACCESS.

(a) Subarea 1.

(1) No accessway to or from the Property is permitted between Stults Road and Old Greenville Avenue. If the existing single family use or structure located on the Property with access to

Greenville Avenue is removed, the driveway connecting that building to Greenville Avenue must be removed, and the curb, gutter, and sidewalk installed.

(2) All entrances to parking areas for a community service center use located on the Property must be closed off when the use is closed to the public.

(b) Subarea 2. The access point on Greenville Avenue is restricted to emergency access only and may count towards the number of access points for a shared access development. (Ord. Nos. 23805; 25850; 32163)

sections.title: Signs
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-393.114. SIGNS.

Signs must comply with the provisions for business zoning districts contained in Article VII. (Ord. Nos. 21918; 25850)

sections.title: Traffic Improvements
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-393.115. TRAFFIC IMPROVEMENTS.

(a) The apportionment of exaction determination must be made prior to issuance of a building permit for new construction for the following off-site traffic improvements at the northwest intersection of Greenville Avenue and Old Greenville Avenue:

(1) Installation of new curb ramps and landing.

(2) Restriping the eastbound Greenville Avenue crosswalk.

(3) Relocating the existing pedestrian push button for minimum PROWAG (Public Right-of-Way Accessibility Guideline) height requirements.

(b) Before the issuance of building permits for new construction, the percentage of the cost to upgrade the off-site traffic improvements in Subsection (a) must be paid to the city as determined by apportionment analysis. (Ord. Nos. 21918; 25850; 32163)

sections.title: Subarea 2 Shared Access Development Provisions
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-393.116. SUBAREA 2 SHARED ACCESS DEVELOPMENT PROVISIONS.

(a) Sidewalks must meet the minimum standards in the Street Design Manual.

(b) Internal street lighting may be provided by lighting standards attached to main structures.

(c) A fence located within the required front yard that surrounds a shared access development must be masonry, wrought iron, or a combination of these materials and may be a maximum eight feet in height. (Ord. Nos. 21918; 25850; 32163)

sections.title: Additional Provisions
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-393.117. ADDITIONAL PROVISIONS.

(a) The Property must be properly maintained in a state of good repair and neat appearance.

(b) Development and use of the Property must comply with all federal and state laws and regulations, and with all ordinances, rules, and regulations of the city. (Ord. Nos. 21918; 25850; 32163)

sections.title: Compliance With Conditions
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-393.118. COMPLIANCE WITH CONDITIONS.

(a) All paved areas, permanent drives, streets, and drainage structures, if any, must be constructed in accordance with standard city specifications, and completed to the satisfaction of the city.

(b) The building official shall not issue a building permit or certificate of occupancy for a use in this PD until there has been full compliance with this article, the Dallas Development Code, the construction codes, and all other applicable ordinances, rules, and regulations of the city. (Ord. Nos. 21918; 25850; 32163)
